- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or volatile, model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows downward momentum.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00 followed by high forecast), especially in 10-15d horizon; cap or smooth out such spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is far above true outcome (e.g., >1.5 units), reduce by 10-20% in next 5d window unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts; use 18d history as anchor for smoothing, especially if sentiment is mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/1.00 alternation, model tends to overfit to recent highs; apply downward bias to 10-15d forecast peaks.
